evidence.text: Management disclosed on 15 Sep (Baird conference) rising hospital and skilled-nursing costs, partly 2025 hospital bills lagging through a claims-system transition. On 9 Oct William Blair downgraded and said it expects Q3 to show cost-trend problems. TD Cowen cut its H2 adj. EBITDA by about $16m on inpatient utilization. That cut takes implied FY EBITDA to roughly $139-141m against the company's $145-163m guide (H2 guide $39-57m). The release is the first quantification: Q3 adj. MBR against the $148-158m adj. gross profit guide, any unfavorable prior-year development (Q2 already carried about $6m), and whether FY EBITDA is cut.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print (Q2 beat, Q3 EBITDA guide soft) fell -20.2%. The 15 Sep conference remarks on costs cost -16% in a session (OCBJ). The April print fell -10.1%. This name has sold guidance and cost disappointments hard, every time over the last four prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -55% since July and the sell-side has cut. What is not priced is the size. No number has been given for the cost overrun or the reserve hit, and if the FY guide were already cut by the company the Street would not be split between -$0.04 and +$0.03. If fully priced, the stock would not have bounced to $8.2 from the $7.5 low, and Cowen would not still say the pressure does not extend into 2027.
evidence.independence: Separate sources point the same way. TD Cowen's H2 EBITDA cut on inpatient utilization (https://www.webull.com/news/15736444743656448, 2026-10-12). William Blair's Q3 cost-trend warning (https://www.tikr.com/blog/alignment-healthcare-sinks-20-as-medicare-plan-downgraded-humana-and-clover-soar, 2026-10-09). The Earnings Whispers preview noting the Q2 unfavorable reserve adjustment (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ALHC/21162). All trace back to the same management disclosure.

evidence.text: The 2027 Star Ratings (released 8 Oct) cut California HMO contract H3815, about 75% of members, from 4.0 to 3.5. Per the company's own 8-K this removes quality bonus payments for FY2028 only, partly offset by provider risk-sharing, with no revenue impact in 2026 or 2027. The company is pursuing appeals and litigation (complaint filed 9 Oct). The call is the first chance to quantify the 2028 hit and the mitigation, and to say whether 2027 bids/benefits change.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the 8-K the stock was -19 to -20% premarket on 9 Oct but closed about -13.4%, then bounced +8.6% on 12 Oct (webull). It now trades about $8.2, above the post-ratings close, so the market has already partly looked through it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Targets were cut to $10-12 and the stock fell double digits. The unpriced residual is only the dollar size of the 2028 QBP loss net of risk-sharing, which the company has not given. A quantified number above or below the roughly 2-3 points of H3815 revenue the Street implicitly assumes could move the stock either way.
evidence.independence: The TIKR article (https://www.tikr.com/blog/alignment-healthcare-sinks-20-as-medicare-plan-downgraded-humana-and-clover-soar) reports the same 8-K plus analyst reactions. One document, so one finding.

evidence.text: The large peers that reported Q3 2026 since ALHC last spoke all came in better than expected on medical costs. UnitedHealth's Q3 MCR was 88.4% against about 89.9% expected, including $610m of favorable 2026 prior-period development (13 Oct). Centene's MLR was 92.7% against 92.84% expected, helped by 'steadier Medicare Advantage results', with guidance raised. Elevance said MA performed better than expected. Industry-wide Q3 MA cost trend looks benign, which bounds how bad an idiosyncratic ALHC overrun is likely to be.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of ALHC trading on peer read-through. ALHC's own cost problem is described by management as company-specific (claims system), which limits transmission.
evidence.why_not_priced: ALHC has not reacted to peers' beats: it is +6.4% over 20 days but -2.3% over 5 days through Elevance and Centene. The Street's ALHC consensus moved to a loss after these peer prints. If the read-through were priced, ALHC estimates would have firmed rather than been cut.
evidence.independence: Centene Q3 beat with steadier MA (https://finimize.com/content/centene-lifted-its-2026-profit-outlook-after-a-big-q3-beat). Elevance MA better than expected (https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/payers/elevance-health-shares-rise-premarket-q3-earnings-revenue-beat). This is a proxy: no direct counterparty of ALHC has confirmed it.

evidence.text: The bar into the print is very low and the setup leans long: Q3 consensus is a loss of -$0.04 (vs +$0.02 a year ago), the stock is -66% from its high, 12.9% of float is short (3.1 days to cover), and the option open interest is 95% calls (put/call OI 0.05). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two upside reactions (+16.5% Feb 2025, +6.0% Jul 2025) came off depressed setups. The four most recent prints were all negative.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown has a named cause, so this is not an unexplained-drawdown claim. The lowered bar is itself what the price reflects. If the market expected an in-guide print, the stock would not trade at 0.15x sales with analysts' targets at $10-12, and Needham would not have initiated at only Hold the day before.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview frames Q3 as a planned dip, -$0.04 consensus (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ALHC/21162, 2026-10-21). It shares the consensus figure with finviz.

first_hunter_context.bar: Revenue consensus $202.10B (Investing.com, https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/amazon-stock-setup-into-todays-earnings-what-could-push-shares-higher-or-lower-93CH-4983838, 2026-10-29) or $202.25B (24/7 Wall St, https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/, 2026-10-29). Both sit at the top of the company's $197.0-202.0B guide (8-K ex99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm, 2026-07-30). EPS consensus is $1.96-1.97, with a range of $1.72-2.32, and is noisy because of non-operating Anthropic and OpenAI marks. Operating income consensus is about $26.2B against a $22.5-26.5B guide. AWS consensus is 37.8-38% YoY, about $45.6-45.7B (FactSet via CNBC; 24/7 Wall St; Yahoo 2026-10-27). Two or more sources agree on each, so the bar counts as sourced.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is about 100-107M shares (~1% of float), with days to cover of 2.25 on 2026-06-15 (Benzinga, https://benzinga.com/quote/AMZN/short-interest) and 2.8 on 2026-07-15 (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/amzn/shortinterest). That is not crowded, and I found no October settlement. I found no 25-delta skew for this event; the baseline file failed (status bars_failed: HTTPError), so it carries no skew, spot or reaction history. The option-implied move is ~6.6% (Bloomberg data via Investing.com, 2026-10-22/29) or ~7.4% (Pepperstone, 2026-10-23). Into the print the stock fell from $262.37 (Oct 21) to $254.60 (Oct 28 close) and was ~$246 midday Oct 29 (-3%) on Alphabet's post-print slide. That is a ~6% drawdown in a week into the print, below the 52-week high of $287.20.

evidence.text: Two peers reported after Amazon last spoke (July 30), and both clouds beat and accelerated well above expectations. Microsoft Azure grew 48% vs 44% expected ($33.17B vs $32.32B), up from 43% the quarter before. Google Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B vs ~90% / $28.7B expected, with TPU systems sales a 'meaningful contributor'. AWS consensus is only 38% (~$45.7B), one point above Q2's 37%, while Jassy said capacity is sold out through 2026 and the backlog is $496B.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: When AWS last surprised (Q2 2026, 37% at its fastest in 18 quarters vs low-30s expected), AMZN rose +15.3% (Pepperstone) to +19.8% (Investing.com) the next day. In Q1 2026, with AWS at 28%, the reaction was +2.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: AWS consensus (FactSet 37.8%) implies roughly +1pt of acceleration. Azure accelerated +5pts and Google Cloud ~+20pts in the same quarter. If the street had marked AWS up to the peers, consensus would sit at 40%+ like BofA's, and AMZN would not have fallen 3% in sympathy with Alphabet the day after the peer prints. But AWS growth is capacity-bound rather than demand-bound, so peer demand transmits only as fast as AWS can add capacity. This is a proxy, which is why it is sized well below the Q2 reaction.
evidence.independence: Alphabet's primary release confirms the Google Cloud figures: $30,709M vs $15,157M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm, 2026-10-28). The AWS backlog of $496B and the 2027 capacity 'lion's share reserved' come from the Amazon Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/amazon-amzn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Both are peer and proxy evidence, not AWS's own Q3 number.

evidence.text: Several sell-side models sit above the 38% AWS consensus going in: BofA (Justin Post) at 40% with a 39% AWS margin, and BNP Paribas at 43-45%. Wells Fargo expects Q4 operating income guidance near the high end.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same AWS line as finding 1: +15 to +20% in Q2 2026 on a beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced: published broker notes are wire copy, and the buy-side whisper likely sits nearer 40% than 38%. That raises the bar a beat must clear for a positive reaction. Kept small for that reason.
evidence.independence: Investing.com 2026-10-29 says the bull case needs ~35%+ growth (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/amazon-stock-setup-into-todays-earnings-what-could-push-shares-higher-or-lower-93CH-4983838). This is a different source from finding 1 but the same AWS line, and is not independent of the peer read-through.

evidence.text: This week's reaction function punished hyperscaler capex and FCF burn even on cloud beats. Alphabet fell ~8% after hours and ~12% midday Oct 29 to $286.17 despite Cloud +103%: Q3 FCF was -$9.07B, capex $51.4B, and EPS of $2.12 missed on an $8.7B equity-securities loss. Amazon is the most exposed to the same verdict: trailing FCF was -$7.6B at June 30, long-term debt was $128.9B (from $65.6B at year-end), the 2026 capex guide of $220B was already raised once for memory costs, and UBS sees spending above $300B by 2027.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (Feb 5, 2026): revenue beat ($213.4B vs $211.3B) but the stock fell 9.7% when the $200B 2026 capex guide overshadowed results (Investing.com table; Morningstar headline). In Q2 2026 the capex raise to $220B came with AWS acceleration and the stock rose 15-20%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: AMZN fell ~3% today in sympathy, and capex/FCF is the most-discussed debate in every preview. The unpriced part is whether Amazon raises 2026 capex again or gives a 2027 number. A capex raise read through Alphabet's verdict would show as a further gap down, which today's -3% has not fully discounted given the 7%+ implied move.
evidence.independence: Alphabet's primary release confirms Q3 FCF of $(9,065)M and capex of $51,355M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm). Amazon's own trailing FCF of -$7.6B is from its Q2 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm). Amazon's 2026 capex guide rose $200B to $220B on memory costs (https://www.fierce-network.com/cloud/memory-drives-amazon-capex-another-20b-2026).

evidence.text: The revenue bar sits at the top of the guide. Consensus of $202.1-202.25B equals the $202.0B top of the $197-202B guide, which carries ~400bp of Prime Day timing drag and ~80bp of FX drag. Amazon beat the top of its revenue guide in Q2 ($200.6B vs a $199B top). Consensus operating income of ~$26.2B sits near the $26.5B top.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Total-revenue beats have not decided the move: Q4 2025 revenue beat ~1% and the stock fell 9.7%; Q1 2026 beat 2.5% and it rose 2.1%; Q3 2025 beat 1.3% and it rose 6.0% (Investing.com table).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the street already models the top of the guide. Only a beat well above $202B (a repeat of Q2's 0.8% over the top) or a miss inside the range would be news. Sized near zero; this lands inside what the company guided.
evidence.independence: Visible Alpha pre-Q consensus of $203.9B revenue and $25.4B operating income, versus the guide (S&P Global, https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/08/amazon-postq-aws-reaccelerates-as-ai-investment-pushes-capex-higher). Shares the guidance document with finding 9.

evidence.text: Peer commentary points to delayed third-party data-centre capacity in the quarter. Microsoft's capex of $45.2B came in under the $50.7B consensus, which it blamed on delayed third-party capacity pushing deliveries into the second half of its fiscal year. Alphabet's capex was also under consensus ($51.36B vs $55.09B). AWS revenue is capacity-gated (Jassy: not enough capacity for 2026 demand), so a similar delay would cap Q3 AWS upside even with demand intact. The offset is lower capex and better FCF.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not directly observed for AMZN; capacity commentary drove the Q2 2026 AWS reacceleration narrative (+15-20%).
evidence.why_not_priced: No preview I found connects the peers' capex shortfalls to AWS revenue timing; previews treat AWS capacity as only growing. Sign is mixed (revenue cap vs FCF relief), so it is sized small and slightly negative.
evidence.independence: Alphabet's capex of $51,355M is confirmed in its 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm). Shares the 24/7 Wall St article with finding 3, but this is a different fact (capex timing vs the FCF reaction).

evidence.text: Prime Big Deal Days (Oct 6-7, 2026), the first data point on Amazon's Q4 that the Q4 guide will be set against: Adobe measured US online spending of $9.86B, +8.5% YoY, slightly below Adobe's own $9.9B / +9.2% forecast.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 guidance and capex together drove the -9.7% in Feb 2026; I could not isolate a reaction to the event data itself.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for three weeks and an industry-wide figure, not Amazon's own sales, so mostly priced. A slight miss against forecast is the only incremental content.
evidence.independence: Forecast comparison from Chain Store Age (https://chainstoreage.com/adobe-prime-big-deal-days-spending-rise-9-99b). Same Adobe dataset.

evidence.text: The digital ad peer read is mixed against Amazon's ad consensus of $20.91B (+18% YoY). Meta's Q3 revenue grew 26.1% to $64.6B. Alphabet's total Google advertising grew only ~11% ($82.0B vs $74.2B), with YouTube ads +9% and Network +1%. Amazon ads grew 26% in Q2, helped by Prime Day falling in that quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ads have been a secondary line; Q2's +26% came alongside the AWS-driven +15-20%. No isolated reaction found.
evidence.why_not_priced: An 18% consensus is an 8pt deceleration from Q2. Prime Day timing explains perhaps 3-5pts of that, so the bar looks modest next to Meta's +26%, but Google's +11% argues the market is not uniformly strong. Net small positive.
evidence.independence: Meta's +26.1% from 24/7 Wall St (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/). Proxy only.

evidence.text: Non-operating marks will make GAAP EPS diverge from the $1.96 consensus (range $1.72-2.32). Q2 carried $53.4B of non-operating gains, mostly Anthropic, and $5.75 EPS. I found no new Anthropic priced round in Q3 (the last was the $965B Series H on 2026-05-28, inside Q2). Amazon funded about $21.3B more of OpenAI after June 30. Alphabet's $8.7B equity-securities loss this quarter cost it $0.55 of EPS and an 'EPS miss' headline that fed its sell-off.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The market looked through Q2's $5.75 vs $1.81 EPS and traded the AWS line instead. Alphabet's equity loss this week coincided with a 12% fall, but alongside a capex/FCF story.
evidence.why_not_priced: Below operating income, with no path to the guide. The sign of any Q3 mark is unknown, since no Q3 priced round was found. [sizing note removed]; it can only distort the headline EPS print for an hour.
evidence.independence: Q2 other income of $53.4B 'primarily from our investments in Anthropic' (Amazon 8-K ex99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm). The OpenAI tranche figure is from Pepperstone (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview).

evidence.text: About $1.2B of Q2 operating income was one-off: ~$600M of tariff refunds, which the CFO called 'the significant majority of refunds we expect', and a ~$551-600M energy-derivative fair-value gain booked mostly in AWS. Q3 guidance assumes no energy-derivative remeasurement. So Q2's 39.4% AWS margin is flattered, and the 39% AWS margin modelled by BofA assumes a repeat.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: AWS margin surprises have mattered for AMZN (Q2's 39.4% was part of the +15-20%), but the one-off component itself has no isolated reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus AWS margin near Q2's level may not strip out the energy gain. A sequential AWS margin dip could read as deterioration. Most of this is remeasurement noise, so sized as a fraction of operating-profit-equivalent dollars.
evidence.independence: The Q3 guide's exclusion of energy-derivative remeasurement is in Amazon's 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm). Shares that document with finding 4.

evidence.text: Financing to fund the capex ramp: Amazon closed four sterling note series on 2026-09-14 (£1.25B 5.200% 2029 plus three £1B series), following USD ($36.9B, March), EUR (March), CAD (C$13.97B, June) and USD (July) offerings. Long-term debt was $128.9B at June 30. The money buys data-centre capacity against a $496B AWS backlog growing at triple digits.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction; debt growth feeds the FCF debate in finding 3.
evidence.why_not_priced: Fully public 8-Ks. The funding is corroborated by the backlog and the sold-out capacity, so per the financing question the sign is zero rather than distress. Its market relevance runs through finding 3, so it is not counted again here.
evidence.independence: Backlog of $496B from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/amazon-amzn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

evidence.text: In September 2026 a federal court approved expanded automatic redress payments under the FTC Prime settlement (users of 11-20 Prime benefits, up to $200 total, payments from Oct 1). More than $845M had been paid by September, from the $1.5B consumer fund accrued with the 2025 settlement.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The original $2.5B FTC charge depressed Q3 2025 operating income (to $17.4B), which makes this quarter's year-on-year comparison easy. No reaction to the expansion found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Likely paid from the existing accrued fund, so there is probably no new charge. If Amazon booked an incremental accrual it falls outside the guide (which excludes legal settlements). [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Fox coverage (https://www.fox5ny.com/news/amazon-settlement-expands-more-money). Same FTC fact.

evidence.text: Company-level forward demand stated on the Q2 call: AWS backlog of $496B (up from ~$364B the quarter before) growing at triple digits YoY. Jassy said 'the lion's share' of planned 2027 AWS capacity is already reserved and that Amazon will not have enough capacity for 2026 demand. Anthropic committed over $100B over 10 years for up to 5GW on AWS, with nearly 1GW before end-2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog disclosure accompanied the Q2 +15-20% reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; it has been public since July 30. The incremental piece is the Q3 backlog print: peers' backlogs (Google ~$514B at Q2) and Azure's acceleration suggest another large step, but that is inference.
evidence.independence: Anthropic's own announcement of the AWS expansion (https://convergedigest.com/anthropic-secures-5-gw-of-ai-compute-in-expanded-100b-aws-deal/). Shares the call transcript with finding 9.

Q2 transplant testing excluding prior-period revenue was $84M, so the guide embeds only about $8M a quarter of catch-up or ASP uplift. At Q2's run rate, Q3 revenue would be about $128-132M against the $122.4M bar.

evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $122.4M sits on the guide midpoint, as if prior-period collections stop. evidence.text: Pinterest has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by a widening margin in both 2026 quarters. Q1: $1,008m against a $951-971m guide (+4.9% vs midpoint, +3.8% vs top). Q2: $1,180m against $1,133-1,153m (+3.2% vs midpoint, +2.3% vs top). The Q3 consensus of $1.20-1.21bn sits at the midpoint-to-top of the $1,190-1,210m guide, so a repeat of even the smaller Q2 overshoot gives ~$1.235-1.24bn, about 2-3% above the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: revenue beat consensus by 2.73% and adj. EPS by 20%, stock -8.68% on a Q3 guide ~1.9% below consensus. May 2026: Q1 beat plus a Q2 guide ~2% above consensus, +6.86%. Nov 2025: revenue in line, weak guide, -21.76%. The reported-quarter beat has not set the sign on any of the last three prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the guide rather than at the guide plus the company's demonstrated overshoot. If the street had priced the pattern, the published Q3 revenue estimate would be ~$1.23bn+ rather than $1.20-1.21bn, and previews would not note that 'a result at the low end of the guided ranges would miss.' Analysts have kept estimates unchanged for 30 days (Yahoo/StockStory 10-27). Buy-side whisper numbers likely carry part of it.
evidence.independence: Q1 overshoot from a separate document, the Q1 2026 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001506293/000150629326000066/q1-26xpressrelease.htm (Q2 guide $1,133-1,153m) and the Q4 2025 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506293/000150629326000019/q4-25xpressrelease.htm (Q1 guide $951-971m). Same company, same habit, two quarters.

evidence.text: The Q4 guide, the line this stock trades on, laps an easy comparison. Q4 2025 revenue grew only 14% (13% constant currency) after the then-CFO said larger US retailers were cutting ad spend under tariff margin pressure, with home-furnishings tariffs adding to it. US & Canada grew just 9% in Q3 2025, then re-accelerated to +13% in Q1 2026 and +18% in Q2 2026. On two-year stacks the August Q3 guide (14% midpoint on a 17% comp) is ~31 points, while the Q4 consensus (~$1.52bn, ~15% on a 14% comp) is only ~29. A Q4 guide on the Q3 guide's stack would be ~17%, about $1.54bn, ~1.5% above consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has set the sign on every recent print. May 2026: guide ~2% above consensus, +6.86%. August 2026: guide ~1.9% below consensus, -8.68%. Nov 2025: Q4 guide midpoint below consensus, -21.76%. Feb 2026: guide below consensus, -16.83%. So roughly 4-8 points per 2% of guide surprise.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market priced the easy comp, Q4 consensus would sit above 15% growth, previews would frame the Q4 guide as a likely beat, and the stock would not have slid 10.8% in five sessions into the print. The TIKR preview (10-26) treats a Q4 guide above ~$1.52bn as the bull case rather than the base case.
evidence.independence: Tariff cause of the weak Q4 2025: TIKR/Barchart coverage of the Nov 2025 call quoting the CFO on 'larger US retailers navigate tariff-related margin pressure', https://www.tikr.com/blog/pinterest-nyse-pins-stock-plunges-over-19-on-q3-earnings-miss-and-weak-forecast. US&C re-acceleration: Q1 and Q2 2026 8-Ks. This is an inference from company numbers; management has not said it.

evidence.text: Europe's headwind does not lap before Q4. The EU replaced the €150 duty exemption with a flat €3-per-item duty on 1 July 2026, and a further handling fee of roughly €2 a parcel is due by 1 November 2026. Ahead of the duty Temu roughly halved and Shein nearly ended their European Google Shopping presence from March. On the Q2 call the CFO said this pressure from Asia-based cross-border retailers continued into Q3. Europe slowed from +27% (Q1) to +12% (Q2) and laps a +41% Q3 2025.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 guide that carried this headwind was cut below consensus and the stock fell 8.68% in August 2026. No prior quarter isolates Europe alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced for Q3, because management flagged it in August. What may not be priced is persistence into Q4, plus the second fee from 1 November. If it were priced, the Q4 consensus would show a Europe deceleration, but that consensus (~15%) does not separate regions. Net of the rest of the company: Europe is ~18% of revenue ($213m of $1,180m in Q2) against US&C at 75% growing 18%, so a 5-point Europe shortfall is under 1 point of total growth.
evidence.independence: CFO comment on continuing Q3 pressure from Q2 call summaries (Yahoo Q2 2026 call summary, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/pinterest-inc-q2-2026-earnings-123000649.html). EU duty start: Euronews 2026-07-01, https://www.euronews.com/2026/07/01/eu-slaps-3-duty-fee-on-shein-temu-and-aliexpress-imports. Europe growth: Q1/Q2 2026 8-Ks.

evidence.text: Meta's Q3 2026 results (10-21) show strong performance-ad demand in the quarter Pinterest is reporting: advertising revenue $63.06bn vs $50.08bn (+26%), ad impressions +10%, average price per ad +14%, and a Q4 revenue guide of $73-76bn with the midpoint above consensus. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline series on peer read-throughs. In August 2026 Pinterest fell 8.68% on its own guide despite a strong ad tape. Meta fell ~7% on its own print (capex and costs), so peer strength has not translated into stock strength this season.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Pinterest rose ~11.9% over the month to 10-27 (Yahoo/StockStory), then gave most of it back. The read-through lands on Q3 revenue and the Q4 guide, while Pinterest's own consensus stayed unchanged for 30 days. If the market had carried it into estimates, the Q3 revenue consensus would have moved above the guide's top.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not a direct counterparty. Alphabet's same-quarter print points the other way (next finding). Deutsche Bank was cited in search-result text as saying digital ad spend ran stronger than expected through Q3, but that was unverified and has no URL, so it is not used.

evidence.text: Alphabet's Q3 2026 release (10-28, after the close) shows Google's ad lines decelerating. Search & other $63.35bn vs $56.57bn (+12%, from +17% in Q2). YouTube ads $11.21bn vs $10.26bn (+9%, from +13% in Q2). Network +1%. Total Google advertising +11% vs +14.5% in Q2. GOOGL fell ~10% after hours on a profit miss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. Historically Pinterest has traded in sympathy with Alphabet's ad revenue surprises, for example +4.5% on an Alphabet ad beat in April 2025 (Reuters via iTiger), but that is a 2025 example.
evidence.why_not_priced: Released the evening before. Pinterest's seal at 17:12 UTC on 10-29 ($20.445) already reflects one session of it, so this is largely in the price by the entry. What remains is whether YouTube's brand/upper-funnel slowdown shows up in Pinterest's Q4 guide.
evidence.independence: Proxy. Points the opposite way to the Meta finding. Pinterest's ads are lower-funnel and shopping-led (Performance+ is 30% of lower-funnel revenue per the CEO at Goldman, per TIKR 10-26), closer to Meta than to YouTube.

evidence.text: James Dibbo became CFO on 2026-10-26, three days before the print. He was VP and CFO of Amazon's Global Entertainment, Advertising and Corporate Development. Julia Brau Donnelly, who resigned 2026-08-26 'to pursue another opportunity' with no disagreement, remains principal financial officer through 2026-10-30. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO-transition print for this company in the baseline. The stock fell ~5-6% on 10-26, the day Dibbo started; QuiverQuant attributes it partly to the transition.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced in the 10-26 drop. The guide-setting risk is not in the published Q4 consensus. If the market expected a reset, the Q4 consensus would have been trimmed; instead estimates stayed flat for 30 days. The new CFO's $9m+ RSU package includes relative-TSR performance shares, which would favour a beatable first guide.
evidence.independence: Departure 8-K 2026-08-26, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506293/000150629326000117/pins-20260826.htm (no disagreement). QuiverQuant 10-26, https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Pinterest+shares+slide+as+investors+position+ahead+of+earnings+and+absorb+CFO+transition (AI-generated attribution). Inference on how a new CFO guides; no document says it.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: March 2026: the Elliott $1bn convert funding a $3.5bn buyback authorization, about +9% premarket (BNN Bloomberg 2026-03-03). No baseline print carried a buyback-only surprise.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nothing has been announced. With the stock back near its H1 buyback average and below the convert price, an accelerated repurchase would be new information. The revolver is financing: it was asked what it buys, and the answer is an upsized backstop with no draw and no distress signal [sizing note removed], so its sign is zero to positive.

evidence.text: PTC's own FY2026 product guide is conservative against what it has already booked. H1 2026 net product revenue was $464.4M (Q1 $225.6M + Q2 $238.8M). The raised $850-950M guide therefore implies H2 of $386-486M, a midpoint of about $218M a quarter, below Q2's $239M. The Street's FY total-revenue consensus of $1.15B sits below the company's own $1.18-1.28B floor. A Q3 product print near the Q2 run rate would force a fourth raise or narrowing, and the market expects that only loosely.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was raised in each 2026 print. Q1 (2026-05-07), raise from $700-800M to $750-850M: +14.27%. Q2 (2026-07-30), raise to $850-950M: -9.94%, sold on decelerating Sephience growth and rising discontinuations. A raise alone does not guarantee an up move on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock has fallen 11.7% since the raise and trades 28.6% below its 52-week high, so the market is not paying for a further raise. If it were, the stock would have held near the post-Q2 high (~$75), and FY consensus would sit inside the guide rather than $30M below its floor. Partly priced: the Earnings Whispers preview names the conservatism explicitly.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-21, gives the FY consensus of $1.15B below the guide and the $218M/qtr implied H2 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/PTCT/21233). The Q1 release gives Q1 product of $225.6M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001070081/000107008126000011/tmb-20260507xex99d1.htm). Shares a document base with the next finding, but lands on a different line.

evidence.text: Sephience patient and revenue run-rate points to a Q3 product beat. Patients on commercial therapy went 946 (2025-12-31) → 1,244 (2026-03-31, +298) → 1,647 (2026-06-30, +403). Revenue per average patient fell from ~$114k to ~$105k a quarter as the international mix rose. At ~+300 net adds and ~$97-100k per patient, Q3 Sephience comes to ~$170-180M (Q2 $151.3M). With Translarna ~$35-45M, Emflaza ~$20M and other ~$20M, product revenue is ~$245-265M. The $311.1M total consensus minus ~$75M royalty implies a product bar of only ~$236M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: Sephience $124.6M (+36% q/q), stock +14.27%. Q2 2026: Sephience $151.3M (+21% q/q), stock -9.94%. Q3 2025: revenue $211.0M vs ~$175.5M consensus, stock +5.98% despite a large EPS miss. This name trades on Sephience q/q growth, and deceleration has been sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: The quarterly consensus implies product revenue roughly flat on Q2. If the market expected $245M+, the preview consensus would not sit at $311M with royalties near $75M, and the stock would not be near its post-Q2 low. This is an inference from company patient counts, not a sourced Sephience estimate. It is capped small because the bar is a single source.
evidence.independence: Q1 release: patients 1,244, Sephience $124.6M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001070081/000107008126000011/tmb-20260507xex99d1.htm). The Q1 call transcript says Japan's first sale came ahead of plan and international will ramp to up to 30 countries by year-end (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/08/ptct-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/). The next finding cuts the other way.

evidence.text: US Sephience new-patient intake has slowed and discontinuation has risen. On the Q1 call (2026-05-08) management said US start forms ran ~140/month and called that a reasonable run rate; cumulative was 1,134 at 2025-12-31 and passed 1,500 in Q1. At the Wells Fargo and Cantor conferences (2026-09-10/11) it said only 'over 2,000' US start forms, which implies ~85-115/month since March, not 140. Discontinuation went from 'low double digits' (Q1 call) to ~20% (Q2 call) to 'stabilizing at 20-25%' (Cantor, 2026-09-11). Slower intake caps Q3 net patient adds and the Q4 exit rate.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print (-9.94%) is the precedent: Sephience growth slowed from +36% to +21% q/q and discontinuation was disclosed at ~20%, and the stock fell despite a guide raise.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was public at three September conferences and the stock fell ~12% after Q2. What is not priced is the Q3 patient-add number that quantifies it. 'Over 2,000' is vague and could hide a number well above 2,000, which is why this is sized smaller than the Q2 reaction.
evidence.independence: Wells Fargo conference summary, 2026-09-10: 'over 2,000' US start forms, discontinuation ~20% (https://quartr.com/events/ptc-therapeutics-inc-ptct-wells-fargo-21st-annual-healthcare-conference_ofWxEewH). Q1 call: ~140/month called a reasonable run rate (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/08/ptct-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/). Earnings Whispers notes discontinuation drifting to ~20% (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/PTCT/21233).

evidence.text: Roche's Evrysdi sales, which drive PTC's royalty line, were flat q/q in Q3. The nine-month total was CHF 1,470M (+18% CER) against H1 CHF 968M, so Q3 was CHF 502M versus CHF 504M in Q2 and CHF 464M in Q1. PTC booked $71.1M of royalty on Q2 and $70.8M in Q3 2025. As tiered royalties step up through the year, Q3 royalty revenue should be ~$70-78M: in line with or slightly above a consensus that implicitly carries ~$75M. The line is non-cash, because the royalty was sold.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The royalty line has never been the driver of a PTCT reaction in the baseline window; the stock trades on Sephience.
evidence.why_not_priced: A counterparty number published after PTC last spoke. It is small and non-cash, so the market has little reason to have moved on it. If it had been read as a large swing, royalty-sensitive estimates would have changed visibly, and no revision was found.

Roche Q1 2026: CHF 464M (https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2026-04-23). PTC Q3 2025 royalty $70.8M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1070081/000107008125000026/tmb-20251104xex99d1.htm).

evidence.text: PTC closed the ST-920 (Fabry gene therapy) acquisition from Sangamo on 2026-09-21, inside Q3: $111M upfront plus up to $100M in approval milestones. As an asset acquisition of a BLA-stage program it will most likely be expensed as acquired IPR&D in Q3, about $1.33 a share. GAAP EPS would then print far below the $0.17 consensus, and the $775-815M GAAP opex guide may be lifted. No path to the revenue guide; it is a one-off below the product line.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: PTC reported EPS of $0.20 against $1.11 consensus and the stock rose +5.98% on revenue, so headline EPS misses have been looked through on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deal is public, so the money is priced. What may not be is whether the $0.17 EPS consensus includes the IPR&D charge. Headline algorithms could react to a large GAAP EPS miss at the release before the call. Small because the history shows EPS misses are ignored.
evidence.independence: August 12, 2026 8-K: closing expected late Q3 or early Q4, $111M upfront (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001070081/000110465926095424/tmb-20260812x8k.htm). evidence.text: Germany's Sephience price negotiation slipped. On the Q1 call (2026-05-08) management expected it to finalize 'this summer'; at Q2 it said Q3 or Q4 2026, and at Wells Fargo (2026-09-10) it was still pending. Under Germany's GKV-FinStG the negotiated reimbursement amount applies retroactively from month 7 after launch, so a settlement in Q3 could bring a catch-up reduction for Germany sales since early 2026. Germany is a small part of the $13M international Sephience revenue in Q1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior PTCT print turned on a European price true-up. The Translarna EU non-renewal in 2025 was a larger, separate event.
evidence.why_not_priced: Whether PTC has accrued for the German discount is not disclosed in the Q2 10-Q text that could be read. A booked catch-up would show as a hit to international Sephience revenue that no preview models. It is small because German volume is small and an accrual may already exist.
evidence.independence: Rule on retroactive application from month 7 (https://go.pharmazie.com/blog/pharma-pricing-germany). Germany price still pending at Wells Fargo (https://quartr.com/events/ptc-therapeutics-inc-ptct-wells-fargo-21st-annual-healthcare-conference_ofWxEewH).

evidence.text: Translarna revenue is lumpy and falling. Q1 2026 was $59.0M, boosted by a large one-time Brazilian government order. Q2 2026 was $42.2M against $59.5M in Q2 2025 and $50.7M in Q3 2025.
